newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil senate approves shipping bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil senate approves shipping bill.

text.p: Brazil's Senate approved a bill opening up river and coastal shipping to foreign companies, a Senate official said Thursday.
The upper house voted in a show of hands to approve the bill, which now has to be sanctioned by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, the official said.
The bill creates the Brazilian Special Register, which entitles foreign shipping companies with Brazilian bases to lower tax and employee contributions.
Companies which qualify under the register must employ Brazilian commanders and chief engineers to run their vessels.
Foreign companies without a base in Brazil may also operate in the country but must employ crews which are two- thirds Brazilian.
The bill, which regulates a constitutional amendment passed in 1995, seeks to increase the number of shipping companies operating in Brazil and reduce the cost of transportation within the country.
